gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Vantrue N4's "4K" is only reachable with the cabin camera switched off (with all three cameras on the front tops out at 1440p, about 44% of the 4K pixel count), or that its $99.99 excludes GPS ($21.99 mount) and parking power ($34.99 kit) while the $72.74 REDTIGER A3 needs a $35.99 kit for parking mode.
standout_why: Compared against Digital Camera World's budget guide (cited; its visible part has no 3-channel camera and no all-cameras-on resolution), deal.ai's 3-channel list (calls the N4 "3-Channel 4K" with 4K in the title only; separates front-alone from three-channel resolution only for the AZDOME M550; no kit prices), my-best's 3-channel list (N4 as 1440p front / 1440p interior / 1080p rear and "you need a separate GPS mount", but no price for it and no word on when 4K applies), Cabin Command, Dash & Drive, Product Bible and offkeytikki (none covers the N4 or A3; Product Bible only gives a general $18 to $50 kit range). Walmart's browse page was walled, so I could not read it; ChatGPT's own answer relayed its N4 listing as 1440p + 1440p + 1080p. So rivals hold the three-channel resolution in part; none has the 4K condition or the priced add-ons.
decides: It confirms rather than overturns the pick. With all three cameras on, the Vantrue N4 and REDTIGER A3 both offer a 1440p-class front and 1080p rear, both use a supercapacitor and both need a roughly $35 hardwire kit for parking mode, so the N4's 4K headline is no reason to pay $27.25 more. The N4 honestly wins on cabin detail (a 1440p cabin mode in the manual, against 1080p on the A3) and a maker-named Sony STARVIS sensor, which is the rideshare segment. It is under $100 only as the bare camera: $121.98 with GPS, $134.98 with parking power, $156.97 with both. The A3 at $72.74 is $108.73 with its kit.
